key_insight: Translation-invariant topological CSS codes decouple into stacks of higher-form toric codes exactly when superlattice translations act trivially on every excitation layer and interlayer gluing vanishes.
engineering_relevance: This criterion and an explicit SUM-and-SWAP circuit construction provide a systematic route to simplifying higher-dimensional codes relevant to fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: Classify excitations into superselection layers and identify translation action and interlayer gluing.
For prime-p codes with m nonzero layers and finitely many excitation types per layer, remove gluing by further coarse-graining by p^(m−1) in every direction once translations act trivially.
Construct a finite-depth, local, CSS-preserving Clifford decoupling circuit, allowing ancillas.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical decoupling criterion, a coarse-graining guarantee, and a constructive algorithm, but no numerical benchmarks or hardware evaluation.
watch_item: Coarse-graining and possible ancilla requirements may introduce practical overhead; the abstract does not quantify circuit resources.
paper_title: Toric codes all the way down: decoupling translation-invariant topological CSS codes in higher dimensions
